textRun.content: Do It Now - Match the key term to its definition
Title: HDI - Measuring Levels of Development
measures gender equality based on the relative gaps between women and men across 4 key areas
the percentage of the population having access to and using improved drinking water sources
an estimate of the average age that members of a particular population group will be when they die.
the number of deaths of infants under 1 year old for every 1,000 live births
the percentage of people in a given area that have relatively simple, stable access to electricity
The amount of money generated by a country per year, as divided equally between each citizen
ratio of the number of people (in a given age group) whose income falls below the poverty line
The proportion of the adult population aged 15 years and over which is literate
HDI Global World Ranking out of 193
All stand up - higher or lower -> if correct stay standing, if incorrect sit down - ‘last man standing’

pageElements.title: How do we measure poverty? | World Vision Australia
pageElements.description:
This animation looks at different ways to measure poverty and human well-being with a special focus on the Human Development Index. This includes measures of income, education and health comparing Australia, Timor Leste and Bangladesh. 

Find out more: https://www.worldvision.com.au/global-issues/work-we-do/poverty
